About me

Technical curiosity, applied responsibly.

I am a Computer Science and Engineering diploma graduate focused on building a career in penetration testing and offensive security.

I am developing practical cybersecurity skills through professional training, hands-on security labs, CTF environments, custom projects, and web application security practice.

My learning covers Linux and Windows privilege escalation, Active Directory security, networking, enumeration, and offensive-security methodology. I value building projects and working through labs alongside theoretical knowledge.

My career direction is penetration testing and red-team operations. I aim to approach every environment with clear scope, careful validation, and useful documentation.

Offensive Security / Red Team

AdversaryForge

Phases 1–10 complete

An enterprise adversary emulation, penetration testing, and purple-team validation lab built for cybersecurity education and authorized security testing in isolated lab environments. It combines a segmented Docker platform (corporate portal, FastAPI API, PostgreSQL, internal Linux engineering service) with a guarded Active Directory deployment foundation and a Python-standard-library assessment engine that runs an authorized attack-path slice, evaluates detection rules against it, validates the detections purple-team style, and generates a professional assessment report.

What changed in Phases 6–10

  • Phase 6Attack-path engine — web entry → API-001 BOLA → LIN01 catalogue → Aurora metadata check, scope-enforced.
  • Phase 79 JSON detection rules — 4 fire in the slice.
  • Phase 8Purple-team validation — TP 4 / FP 0 / FN 0.
  • Phase 9HTML + Markdown report from a real run — 1 validated high finding (BOLA, API-001, CWE-639, OWASP API1:2023, MITRE T1213).
  • Phase 10Hardening and docs — 44 new tests pass.

Phases 1–10 are complete as a lab implementation; live Active Directory validation is still pending.

Ferrow Dynamics

Custom lab · Hard

A custom TryHackMe-style security challenge environment (developed from the BlackVault VM) designed to support multi-stage offensive-security learning. The lab focuses on architecture, challenge design, reconnaissance, service and web enumeration, multiple footholds, Linux access, web exploitation, privilege escalation, and multiple attack paths. Public material intentionally excludes flags, credentials, private keys, and solution details.
